title: Demo-mode bulk-reject clicks fall through to the real live bulk-reject API endpoint
detail: In demo mode these clicks POST to the live /api/v1/vacancies/:id/applications/bulk-reject with csrf "demo-csrf-token". Server rejects it (anon: no session; logged-in: CSRF mismatch + vacancy scoping), so no mutation is possible — but demo mode does issue a real write attempt, violating the no-writes pillar, and the demo/ grep lint cannot catch it (call site is client.gleam).
recommended_fix: Add arms for UserClickedMarkSelectedRejected and UserClickedMarkAllRejected in demo_update.handle that route through the existing demo_api.bulk_reject_applications so the mutation stays in the in-memory store.

title: Rejected-applicant fixture uses famous real person's name ("Grace Kelly") attached to a CCJ/possession-order story
evidence: const app_grace_json = "{\"id\":\"a-grace\",...\"first_name\":\"Grace\",\"last_name\":\"Kelly\",...\"is_smoker\":true,\"has_eviction_history\":true,\"eviction_details\":\"Rent arrears, possession order settled in 2024\",\"has_ccjs\":true,...\"status\":\"rejected\"...}"
detail: Spec requires fixtures be obviously synthetic with no real persons. "Grace Kelly" is a globally famous real (deceased) person; attaching her name to a rejected applicant with a possession order, CCJ and smoking flag is a reputational/taste risk on a public marketing surface.
recommended_fix: Rename the fixture to a clearly fictional name (e.g. "Gráinne Keogh") and regenerate the corresponding pre-baked PDF (report-a-grace.pdf) and report_filenames() entry to match.
